q:
1. Which of the following is/are the major features of the foreign policy of Nepal?
1. Non-alignment
2. Neutrality
3. Traditional diplomacy
4. Principle of Panchasheel
explain: Nepal's foreign policy is strictly guided by the principles of Non-alignment and the five principles of Panchasheel as enshrined in its Constitution.

q: 2. When did Nepal establish diplomatic relation with America?
explain: Nepal established diplomatic relations with the United States on April 25, 1947, making it the second country to do so.

q: 3. When is World Post Day observed?
explain: The day is observed because the Universal Postal Union (UPU) was established on 9 October 1874. The 2026 (152nd) theme: 'One Postal Network, Infinite Possibilities'. Nepal obtained membership on 11 October 1956 (B.S. 2013 Asoj 26).

q: 4. In which year, the millennium development goals (MDGs) declared by the United Nations (UN)?
explain: The MDGs were established following the Millennium Summit of the United Nations in 2000.

q: 5. The United Nations Charter was signed in which of the following cities?
explain: The UN Charter was signed on June 26, 1945, in San Francisco at the conclusion of the United Nations Conference on International Organization.

q: 6. Which of the following is not the purpose of the UN?
options: To develop friendly relationship among nations on the basis of equality
To be a centre for harmonizing the action of nations
To achieve international cooperation in resolving economic problems of the world
To maintain international peace and security
explain: While the UN acts as a center for harmonizing actions, the specific wording of the question asks for the primary 'purpose' excluding others; option (b) is often considered a 'method' rather than a 'prime goal' compared to peace and security.

q: 7. How many articles are there in United Nation's Charter?
explain: The official UN Charter consists of 111 articles.

q: 8. Which organ of the United Nations Organizations is responsible for coordinating the work its specialized agencies?
explain: ECOSOC (Economic and Social Council) coordinates the economic, social, and related work of the 15 UN specialized agencies.

q: 9. Which is the first country whose membership of UNO was dissolved?
explain: In 1971, the UN General Assembly recognized the People's Republic of China as the only legitimate representative of China to the UN, effectively expelling the representatives of Taiwan (Republic of China).

q: 10. Which of the following is the main body of the United Nation organization?
explain: The General Assembly is considered the main deliberative, policymaking, and representative organ of the UN.

q: 11. Which General Assembly was conducted as the millennium General Assembly by UNO?
explain: The 55th session of the UN General Assembly in 2000 was designated as the 'Millennium Assembly'.

q: 12. Which countries are the Permanent of the Security Council of UNO?
explain: The 'P5' are China, France, Russian Federation, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

q: 13. Nepal had been the temporary member of UN Security Council for ____ tenure.
explain: Nepal has served as a non-permanent (temporary) member of the Security Council twice: 1969-1970 and 1988-1989.

q: 14. The total number of members in Security Council of UN?
explain: The Security Council consists of 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.

q: 15. How many temporary members should be there in the provision of UNO Security Council?
explain: The UN Charter provides for 10 non-permanent (temporary) members, elected for two-year terms.

q: 16. How many member counties are there in UNHCR?
explain: The Executive Committee of the High Commissioner's Programme (ExCom) governs UNHCR, and as per recent records in the text, it consists of 58 member countries (though this number has grown over time, we stick to the provided options).

q: 17. Who are the members of the General Assembly?
options: All members of the United Nations
All members of the Security Council
Permanent members of the Security Council
Members of the Economic and Social Council
explain: Every member state of the United Nations is represented in the General Assembly.

q: 18. Who was the first Secretary General of UNO?
explain: Trygve Lie of Norway was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations, serving from 1946 to 1952.

q: 19. Who was the first Secretary General of UNO to Visit in Nepal?
explain: U Thant of Burma (Myanmar) was the first UN Secretary-General to visit Nepal in 1967.

q: 20. Basel convention is related to the --------
options: Trans-boundary Movements of the Hazardous wastes and their disposal
explain: The Basel Convention (1989) regulates the international trade and disposal of hazardous wastes.

q: 21. When did international labor organization (ILO) received the Nobel Peace Prize?
explain: The ILO was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969 on the occasion of its 50th anniversary.

q: 22. In which city was the South Asian Preferential Trading Agreement (SAPTA) negotiated and signed on April 11, 1993?
explain: SAPTA was negotiated and signed in Dhaka, Bangladesh, on April 11, 1993, during the 7th Summit. The other options hosted different summits.

q: 23. What is the first specialized agency of UNO?
explain: The International Labour Organization (ILO), established in 1919, became the first specialized agency of the UN in 1946.

q: 24. Which country was the last to ratify the SAPTA agreement on November 5, 1995?
explain: Bangladesh was the final country to ratify SAPTA on November 5, 1995. The other options ratified earlier.

q: 25. How many Articles are contained in the SAPTA Agreement charter?
explain: There are exactly 25 Articles in the SAPTA Charter. Ten refers to the main SAARC Charter; Fourteen refers to the goods scheduled.

q: 26. WTO came into existence in the year ----------
explain: The World Trade Organization was established on January 1, 1995, following the Marrakesh Agreement.

q: 27. Which among the following is not a specialized agency of the United Nations Organization?
explain: While the WTO works closely with the UN, it is an independent organization and not a 'specialized agency' in the formal legal sense.

q: 28. On which date did the SAFTA agreement officially enter into force?
explain: SAFTA officially entered into force on January 1, 2006. January 6, 2004 is the signing date; November 29, 2012 is SATIS's active date.

q:
29. Match the Group I with Group II and choose the correct answer.
**Group I:** (a) ICAO (b) FAO (c) IMF (d) ILO
**Group II:** (1) Canada (2) Italy (3) USA (4) Switzerland
explain: ICAO is in Canada, FAO is in Italy, IMF is in USA, and ILO is in Switzerland.

q: 30. Which of the following UN agencies has received Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 A.D.?
explain: The World Food Programme (WFP) was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for its efforts to combat hunger.

q: 31. Which of the following agencies assesses the "LDC Graduation"?
explain: LDC graduation is monitored by the Committee for Development Policy (CDP) under the UN Economic and Social Council.

q: 32. When was the Convention on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women issued?
explain: The CEDAW convention was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1979.

q: 33. As of August, 2024, there are ____ member states as the parties on UN convention against Corruption.
explain: As per the updated records provided, 191 states are parties to the UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC).

q: 34. The United Nations General Assembly has declared 2023 as the -------
options: International Year of Fruits and Vegetables
explain: The UN General Assembly declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets to raise awareness of the health and nutritional benefits of millets.

q: 35. Which period was declared to mark as "World Decade of Indigenous Language" by United Nations?
explain: The UN declared 2022-2032 as the International Decade of Indigenous Languages to draw attention to the endangerment of many indigenous languages.

q: 36. Nepal was attained membership of UNO in ---------
explain: Nepal became a member of the United Nations on 14 December 1955, after its earlier applications were vetoed.

q: 37. In which country did Nepal work as a peacekeeper for the first time under the United Nations?
explain: Nepal's first deployment as a UN peacekeeping troop contributor was in Lebanon.

q: 38. According to UN Peacekeeping Missions Report -2023, Nepal is the ____ largest troops Contributing Country in UN Peace keeping Operations.
explain: As per the 2023 UN Peacekeeping report referenced here, Nepal ranked as the top (1st) troop-contributing country.

q: 39. When was Nepal became the member of World Trade Organization (WTO)?
explain: Nepal became a member of the WTO on 23 April 2004, becoming the first Least Developed Country to join through full accession negotiations.

q: 40. Who was the first Secretary General of SAARC?
explain: Abul Ahsan of Bangladesh served as the first Secretary-General of SAARC from 1985 to 1989.

q: 41. Among the following South Asian Counties, Nepal first established diplomatic relation with:
explain: Among the given options, Nepal's diplomatic relationship with Afghanistan predates its ties with the other listed countries.
